---
title: "06 · Practice — Polynomial Algorithms"
---

These exercises begin where a tested polynomial library ends: each requires a
modelling step or a non-obvious use of polynomial machinery.

## Solved exercises

### A. Samples are not a degree bound

Recover a polynomial of degree at most two from values 1, 6, 17 at 0, 1, 2.
Give a different polynomial with the same samples when the bound is removed.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
The second finite difference determines twice the quadratic coefficient.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Solution"}
Writing $f=a+bx+cx^2$ gives $a=1$, $b+c=5$, $2b+4c=16$, hence
$c=3,b=2$. Thus $f=1+2x+3x^2$. The polynomial $f+x(x-1)(x-2)$
has the same samples but degree three. These computations require rational
arithmetic or a field in which 2 is a unit; in characteristic two the sample
points 0 and 2 coincide.
:::

### B. A false CRT shortcut

An integer convolution coefficient is known only to lie in $[0,100]$.
Can its residue modulo 17 determine its residue modulo 10?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Find two bounded numbers agreeing modulo 17.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Solution"}
No: 1 and 18 agree modulo 17 but differ modulo 10. Auxiliary CRT moduli
must have product greater than 100 for unambiguous reconstruction on this
interval. Garner's algorithm changes representation, not this information limit.
:::

### C. Sum of pair differences

Two multisets contain nonnegative integers at most $D$. Derive all counts of
ordered pairs $(a,b)$ with difference $a-b=d$ for $-D\le d\le D$.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Reverse the second frequency array and solve its convolution index equation.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Solution"}
Let $u_i$ count first-multiset values $i$ and $v_{D-j}$ count second-multiset
values $j$. Index $i+D-j=D+d$ counts exactly the desired pairs, so answer $d$
is $(u*v)_{D+d}$. The range 0…2D includes every difference. Complexity is
$O(M(D+1))$ after frequency construction; multiply occurrence counts, not mere
presence flags. Diagonal pairs are included when the multisets coincide unless
the problem explicitly excludes reusing one occurrence.
:::

## 1. AtCoder ABC 196 F — Substring 2 (`Advanced`)

- [Statement](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc196/tasks/abc196_f) ·
  [official editorial](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc196/editorial/952) · English/Japanese
- Train: turn mismatch counts at every alignment into correlations.

<details><summary>Hint 1</summary>Encode zeros and ones separately.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2</summary>Reverse the pattern so every alignment is a convolution coefficient.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3</summary>Count equal pairs, then subtract from pattern length.</details>

## 2. AtCoder ABC 260 Ex — Colorfulness (`Mastery`)

- [Statement](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc260/tasks/abc260_h) ·
  [official editorial](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc260/editorial/4469) · English/Japanese
- Train: merge rational generating functions and invert a denominator.
- Prerequisites: [inclusion–exclusion](../04-combinatorics/chapter.qmd),
  [labelled generating functions](../08-generating-functions/chapter.qmd),
  and [FPS inversion](../07-formal-power-series/chapter.qmd). This is a return exercise.
- First derive the distribution $a_k$ of colorfulness by selecting equal-adjacent
  pairs and applying marked binomial inversion. The hints below address the
  second stage after that distribution is known.

<details><summary>Hint 1</summary>Write the OGF of $\sum a_k k^{n}$ as a sum of simple fractions.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2</summary>Merge fractions with a divide-and-conquer product tree.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3</summary>After obtaining $S(x)/T(x)$, invert $T$ and convolve.</details>
